title: Radio arranging pace: Bargy and Hayden versus Grofe and Challis
summary: Bargy and Hayden turned out many fast arrangements for extra pay while Challis and Grofe plodded along at two a week.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Now, he had to look forward to the radio business. The dance business had gone by and in this radio thing, you know, we weren't -- Ferde and I both, we were not used to that either. We were not you know, "Get this out by 8 o'clock." We were not used to that sort of thing. Barby and Lenny, they were doing five, six arrangements a week. Take a print, cut and paste, take it and throw it together and you take a chorus, I'll take a chorus," that was not the kind of thing that we were used to doing.

Ferde was used to trying to make his stuff, I was used to trying to do mine, and we hadn't for quite some time now, we hadn't been doing things like that, but these guys were now doing a radio type of show which the idea was to make enough arrangements. Paul was paying them 50 bucks for every arrangement, besides their salary and they were making -- in

those days, 300 bucks easily every week, over their salary and the other things that they would do. They were busy enough but they could take that, both of them. They were great at it. Ferde and I were still plodding along on our two a week.
So that's the way it ended, with the Whiteman. Went up to hear the band when we were up in Pelham a couple of times. That was the end.
